A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Takin-VC and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and references supporting comparison. All 20 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2 were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 report original voice-conversion experiments, listener ratings, objective measurements, gender comparisons, speaker-embedding visualization, and component ablations in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: Sections 4–5 retain original empirical evaluations and report additional baseline comparisons, inference-efficiency measurements, and component ablations in Tables 1–4.

M1.justification: V1 Equation 1 uses learned additive mixing of PPG and quantized SSL features followed by convolution and ReLU. V2 instead multiplies PPGs by projected quantized WavLM features using LeakyReLU, substantively changing the encoder's fusion operation. However, v2 Section 4.4 still describes weighted summation, leaving an implementation inconsistency.

E1.justification: Both versions use LibriTTS and the approximately 500k-hour Mandarin/English corpus, retain the 100-speaker evaluation population, and evaluate the same four gender-conversion directions. The new emphasis on expressive speech is not accompanied by a distinct dataset or targeted test scenario.

E2.justification: V2 Table 1 adds evaluated StableVC and SeedVC baselines alongside DiffVC, NS2VC, VALLE-VC, and SEFVC. This substantively broadens the central comparison to include style-controllable VC and diffusion-transformer VC systems.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 changes the reported inference range from 15–50 to 5–20 steps and the setting used for tabulated results from 50 to 10 steps. V2 also introduces real-time factor as an evaluation metric. These are reported protocol changes; the PDFs do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 refines the hybrid-versus-ASR ablation into separate PPG-removal and SSL-removal tests and adds removal of the entire context-aware module. Voiceprint and memory removals, gender comparisons, and the t-SNE analysis remain. This is a focused extension of the existing component-validation analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% confidence intervals for subjective scores in Table 1 and retain the same uncertainty-reporting convention in ablations. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, significance tests, or new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds StableVC and SeedVC results, an RTF column reporting 0.154 for Takin-VC, and new or revised ablation results. The ASR-only comparison changes from the 'w/o hybrid' row to an explicitly HybridFormer-only 'w/o SSL' row with different scores. Existing Table 1 quality scores and Table 2 values remain numerically unchanged, but the revised method and inference budget prevent same-setting cross-version performance claims.

T1.justification: V2 adds Section 3.5 and Equation 5 defining a weighted CFM-plus-RVQ commitment objective, and revises Equation 1's mathematical fusion definition. The optimal-transport flow formulation and Equations 2–4 otherwise remain substantially unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, contributions, and conclusion shift from general zero-shot conversion quality toward expressive speech preservation. V2 newly claims firstness in maintaining highly expressive paralinguistic characteristics, including crying and breathing, and extends its comparative superiority claims to expressiveness and inference speed.

C2.justification: V2 adds a gradient-based explanation for preserving paralinguistic information and interprets the new ablations as evidence concerning timbre leakage and context-aware modeling. V1's Discussion and Limitations section disappears, including its speech-editing boundary, misuse discussion, and data-efficiency interpretation.

D1.justification: V2 specifies the fusion activation's negative slope of 0.2, the commitment-loss weight of 0.01, and four self-attention blocks in the memory-module description. V1's four-second reference-duration disclosure disappears, and the demo link changes host. Most hardware, optimizer, and codebook details remain.

R1.justification: The new claim of being the first approach to preserve highly expressive speech substantially changes positioning relative to prior work. V2 adds CTEFM-VC, StableVC, and SeedVC citations while trimming discussion of few-shot/one-shot VC, CycleGAN approaches, and ELaTE. The broad SSL, diffusion, and language-model background remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, background, method explanations, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Memory and context-aware subsections are reordered, a training-objective subsection is added, and the Discussion and Limitations section is removed. These changes substantially reorganize the narrative.

P2.justification: The overview and timbre-module diagrams are substantially redrawn, and the standalone two-stage encoder diagram disappears. Table 1 gains baseline rows and an RTF column; ablations are split into content and timbre tables. The retained t-SNE visualization is enlarged and restyled, becoming Figure 4 instead of Figure 5.

improvement.justification: Added baselines, RTF measurements, finer component ablations, and explicit loss documentation strengthen the paper. However, v2 introduces central expressive-speech superiority and firstness claims without a dedicated evaluation, and its multiplicative fusion definition conflicts with Section 4.4's retained summation description. These gains and unresolved weaknesses prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
